subject: Re: MAP & staged private offer — EdgeScale evaluation & commit schedule
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Kristen Park <kristen@edgescale.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP kickoff — evaluation milestones + staged private offer direction

Kristen — great to meet last week. As discussed, attaching an initial Mutual Action Plan that ties your evaluation milestones to a staged AWS private offer and corresponding commit/discount steps. High-level goal: let EdgeScale run a production-like pilot (up to 100 concurrent inference qps) during the 8-week evaluation, with discounts that unlock as you hit milestone gates.

Attached: 20270214-EdgeScale-MAP-v1.pdf (MAP draft), which contains:
- Week-by-week evaluation milestones (sandbox access, integration test, latency/load validation, pilot signoff)
- Credit drawdown schedule (developer credits up front, production credits on milestone pass)
- Private offer triggers: Stage 1 (pilot) -> Stage 2 (ramp) -> Stage 3 (commit) with suggested commit bands and discount tiers

Questions for this thread:
1) Can EdgeScale accept an AWS private offer as the preferred billing vehicle (we will coordinate the private offer with AWS marketplace)?
2) For milestone acceptance, do you want engineering signoff + product PO, or procurement-only signoff?
3) Any constraints on timing for your legal review / procurement cycle we should factor into the MAP?

Next step: Jordan and Marcus will draft the AWS private offer term sheet that mirrors the MAP commit bands and credits. If this looks good, we’ll propose a PO template for procurement to speed close.

Thanks —
Lauren
Lauren Bishop | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134
Redwood Inference

From: Kristen Park <kristen@edgescale.com>

Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@edgescale.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — evaluation milestones + staged private offer direction

Lauren — thanks for the doc and outline. Quick answers:
- Yes, we prefer an AWS private offer for billing; our procurement will only sign via marketplace offers.
- Milestone acceptance: product/engineering signoff + procurement approval for the PO. Engineering needs to see clear SLOs for throughput and cost per inference.
- Legal timeline: procurement needs ~3 weeks for standard review; if there are material contract changes it may be longer.

Couple of asks before we move forward:
1) Can you include an explicit SLA / measurable performance acceptance criteria in the MAP? Token-level latency percentiles and cost per 1M tokens would help.
2) We will need an itemized credit schedule that ties credits to milestone acceptance (not just discounts).

I’ll loop procurement on the next email.

—Kristen
Kristen Park | Head of Product, EdgeScale
kristen@edgescale.com

Team — attaching an updated MAP that includes measurable acceptance criteria and an AWS private offer term sheet draft that mirrors the commit bands. High level changes:
- Acceptance criteria added: 99th pct token latency < 250 ms at 100 qps, median cost per 1M tokens <= $35 during pilot.
- Credit schedule: $25k engineering credits at contract signature; $50k production credits released on pilot signoff; further credits released as commit tranches are hit.
- Private offer term sheet (attached) maps commits to marketplace SKUs and discount tiers; includes monthly commit cadence and overage pricing.

Attachments: 20270214-EdgeScale-MAP-v1.pdf (updated), 20270218-Redwood-AWS-PrivateOffer-TermSheet.pdf (draft).

Kristen — can procurement confirm that a private offer with staged commit tranches and credit drawdown is acceptable? If procurement prefers upfront PO + net-30 vs marketplace bill-by-SKU we can model both.

Next actions: Jordan will prepare a concise PO template, Marcus will coordinate with AWS AM to provision the private offer, and I’ll track legal redlines. Target: procurement signoff by 3/10 to hit our Q1 close.

Thanks —
Lauren

Attachment: 20270218-Redwood-AWS-PrivateOffer-TermSheet.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 14:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: procurement checklist + possible concessions

Lauren / Marcus — internal note on procurement items EdgeScale usually flags and proposed concessions we can offer without moving list price too much: 

Procurement checklist (likely asks):
- Proof of SOC2 & data flow diagrams (we have SOC2 report on S3 link)
- Clarify data retention and keys (offer customer-managed KMS option for private deployment)
- Termination/exit assistance for pilot -> production (help migrate KV cache / exported prompts)
- Clear billing vehicle: private offer via AWS Marketplace with PO referencing offer id

Concessions we can offer to speed:
- 6 months of increased trial credits (extra $25k) if they sign within 3 weeks of pilot signoff
- One-time engineering kickoff day (remote) to validate integration
- 30-day SLA credit buffer: if 99th pct latency breaches SLA for >3 days, provide token credits as remediation (capped)

I also attached a redlines summary we should expect from legal. Marcus — can you coordinate with AWS AM to confirm the private offer flow for staged SKUs?

—Jordan

Attachment: contract-redlines-edgescale-20270222.pdf (PDF stub)

Hi Lauren / team — procurement here. Thanks for the updated MAP and term sheet. A few items before we can route to legal: 

1) Please provide a short (1-page) summary that maps MAP milestones to exact marketplace SKUs and billing events. We need to present that to finance.
2) We prefer marketplace billing (private offer) but will accept a PO referencing the offer if you can provide an invoice schedule. Net-30 acceptable.
3) Legal asks: standard liability limits + data handling language; we will push on the SLA credit mechanism to convert into a service credit line (not token credits) — ok to discuss.

If you can get the one-page mapping and an updated private offer term sheet that reflects invoice cadence, we can turn this to legal the week of 3/8. Our target internal signoff is 3/19.

Thanks —
EdgeScale Procurement
